fatal_errors: The proposed thermomechanical bimodal-grain treatment does not reconstruct the target HPHT treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
It replaces the target FCC/B2 lamellar-to-hierarchical transformation and coherent-interface mechanism with an unrelated fine/coarse grain-size mechanism.
The cited evidence does not directly support formation or performance of the proposed graded bimodal microstructure; E2 instead concerns a fine lamellar FCC/B2 eutectic high-entropy alloy.
No target-specific quantitative outcome, pressure dependence, interface coherence, deformation modes, or fracture/GND signatures are predicted.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general strength–ductility trade-off and proposes a scientifically plausible heterogeneous-grain strategy. Its controlled comparison and explicit falsification rule make the alternative experimentally testable. However, it fails to identify the target material, HPHT intervention, processing conditions, hierarchical coherent-interface structure, dislocation-transfer mechanism, and quantitative strength/elongation gains. The boundary statement is generic and does not distinguish HPHT from lower-pressure HIP or thermomechanical processing. Evidence discipline is weak because the supplied citations establish the general challenge and an FCC/B2 eutectic-alloy strategy, but not the claimed bimodal-grain intervention.
